mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in payroll employment growth above 150k signals improved labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where PAYEMS growth exceeds 150k (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the Housing Starts Index below 1.2 million units signals weakening residential demand, which reduces construction-related earnings and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when HOUST falls below 1.2m for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month contraction in the Industrial Production Index below 0.5% signals manufacturing weakness, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when INDPRO growth is below 0.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures below 2% signals weakening demand, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when RSAFS growth is below 2% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals labor market overheating, which increases wage pressures and raises recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in GDP growth below 1% while Housing Starts remain above 1.2 million signals broad demand weakness outside housing, which reduces corporate earnings and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 3-month delta < 1.0 and HOUST > 1200000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when GDP growth is below 1% and HOUST remains above 1.2m for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
